stories.title: The Com: the global cybercrime network posing a ‘chilling threat’ to children
summary: FBI estimates thousands of people identify as members, or recent members, of group linked to indecent images of girls and blackmailIt sounds benign: the Com, short for the Community.

But crime agencies around the world warn that it is far from that and the young cybercriminals involved are causing havoc and putting children at chilling, sickening risk.Beau-Jack Mensforth was jailed by a UK judge on Friday for his activities as part of the Com.

He was one individual operating from his bedroom in north-east England, but there are probably thousands more like him and parents are being urged by police to be aware and to check their children’s devices.

stories.title: Jared Kushner’s 70-minute interview reveals perils of treating Putin like a corporate rival
summary: Trump’s son-in-law and senior negotiator paints Russian invasion of Ukraine as a misunderstanding to be resolvedIn the space of a 70-minute interview, Jared Kushner – Donald Trump’s son-in-law and a prominent US negotiator in Russia, Gaza and Iran – probably did more to reveal why the world is mired in entrenched conflicts than a thousand geopolitical tomes or seminars.During the conversation this week with Mathias Döpfner, the chief executive of the Axel Springer media publisher, Kushner gave a rare insight into his diplomatic technique, offering a string of homilies that veered close to banalities: “You have nothing until you have something”, “diplomacy is like untying knots on a fishing line for his son”, and “you play the ball from where it lands”.

stories.title: Newly released documents suggest CIA did more post-9/11 waterboarding than previously acknowledged
summary: Declassified documents appear to support belief that waterboarding was more common and may have occurred beyond two acknowledged sitesNewly released documents suggest that the CIA waterboarded more detainees during the post-9/11 “war on terror” than previously acknowledged, utilizing a site north of Kabul, Afghanistan, for the practice of simulated drowning.The agency has acknowledged waterboarding three men: Abu Zubaydah, believed to be a high-ranking member of al-Qaida; Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, suspected architect of the 11 September 2001 attacks; and Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri, accused of planning the 2000 bombing of a navy destroyer.
